answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and thus paying the timber bond on all of them and exposing each to the cipher slash. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 2 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Because the echo audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Honest users pay that once, farms 29 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
